events.title: Giordano Bruno Burned at the Stake
events.description: The Italian philosopher, astronomer and former friar was executed for heresy in Rome's Campo de' Fiori. He had defended the idea of an infinite universe filled with countless worlds.
events.significance: Bruno became a lasting symbol of free thought and the clash between inquiry and religious authority in the early modern era.

events.title: Molière Dies After Performing
events.description: The French playwright, actor and comic master died in Paris. He collapsed while performing in his own play, The Imaginary Invalid.
events.significance: Molière's satires, including Tartuffe and The Misanthrope, shaped European comedy. French is often called the language of Molière.

events.title: Jefferson Wins the Presidency in a House Vote
events.description: The Electoral College had tied Thomas Jefferson and Aaron Burr. After days of deadlock, the House of Representatives chose Jefferson as president and made Burr vice president.
events.significance: The crisis led to the 12th Amendment, which gave electors separate ballots for president and vice president. It also showed a peaceful transfer of power between rival parties.

events.title: The H. L. Hunley Sinks the USS Housatonic
events.description: During the American Civil War, the Confederate submarine H. L. Hunley attacked the Union warship USS Housatonic off Charleston, South Carolina, and sank it.
events.significance: It was the first time a submarine sank an enemy warship, and it foreshadowed the role of undersea warfare in later conflicts.

events.title: Michael Jordan Is Born
events.description: Michael Jordan, the future basketball star, was born in Brooklyn, New York.
events.significance: Jordan won six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls and became one of the most recognizable athletes in history. He helped turn the NBA into a global brand.
